worldcombat.skill.celebrate.summary: Throws a party for its very happy trainer: confetti and streamers burst out, and every friendly nearby (itself included) is caught up in it, carrying a Celebrating status. The Cheer form pumps them up (Speed +1 stage); the Treat form hands out a share of health. It does nothing at all to enemies.
worldcombat.skill.celebrate.use.0: Lift the whole team before a group fight starts
worldcombat.skill.celebrate.use.1: Hand the team a share of health to breathe in a bad spot
worldcombat.skill.celebrate.use.2: Fill a circle with morale for very little cost
Confetti spreads to a radius of %1$s blocks, and every friendly inside (itself included) carries the Celebrating status for %2$s.
worldcombat.skill.celebrate.vigor.on: Treat form: each one recovers %1$s of its own max health; this party gives no Speed.
worldcombat.skill.celebrate.vigor.off: Cheer form: each one gains +1 Speed stage; this party restores no health.
Wind-up %1$s s, recovery %2$s s, cooldown %3$s s; the move is cheap enough to use often.
worldcombat.skill.celebrate.timing: The party reaches %1$s blocks; wind-up %2$s s, recovery %3$s s, %4$s PP and cooldown %5$s s from commit. It only affects friendlies.
worldcombat.skill.celebrate.preference.v: On (Treat): every friendly caught recovers a share of its own max health, but gains no Speed. Off (Cheer): everyone gains +1 Speed stage, but no health is restored. Each direction has its moment.
worldcombat.skill.celebrate.preference.a: The partner only considers throwing a party while a threat is this close; larger starts it earlier and exposes the partner more.
At least this many friendlies (itself included) must be nearby to celebrate; 1 parties even alone, larger waits for a crowd.
When on, the partner will also leave its post to throw a party for the team.
